title: Subscription Expiry and Days Remaining
description:
For each subscription calculate the expiry date (start date + 30 days) and how many days remain until expiry as of `2026-09-24`.

**Table: subscriptions** — `id`, `customer_id`, `plan`, `start_date`

Output columns: `customer_id`, `plan`, `start_date`, `expiry_date`, `days_remaining`. Order by `expiry_date`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE subscriptions (id INT, customer_id INT, plan VARCHAR, start_date DATE); INSERT INTO subscriptions VALUES (1,101,'Basic','2026-09-10'),(2,102,'Pro','2026-09-05'),(3,103,'Basic','2026-09-15'),(4,104,'Enterprise','2026-09-01'),(5,105,'Pro','2026-09-18'),(6,106,'Basic','2026-09-20'),(7,107,'Enterprise','2026-09-12'),(8,108,'Pro','2026-09-22');
solution_sql: SELECT customer_id, plan, start_date, start_date + INTERVAL '30 days' AS expiry_date, (start_date + INTERVAL '30 days') - DATE '2026-09-24' AS days_remaining FROM subscriptions ORDER BY expiry_date

test_cases.description: 8 subscriptions each with a computed expiry_date and days_remaining (may be negative for expired ones)

hints: Add INTERVAL '30 days' to a DATE column to get the expiry date.
Subtract two DATE values to get the number of days between them; negative results mean the subscription has already expired.
explanation: start_date + INTERVAL '30 days' shifts each date forward by 30 days. Subtracting a reference date (2026-09-24) from expiry_date gives days remaining. Customer 104 started 2026-09-01 → expires 2026-10-01 → 7 days remaining. Customer 101 started 2026-09-10 → expires 2026-10-10 → 16 days remaining. Negative values indicate expired subscriptions.
